entries.subject: The unchanged wooden school blackboard with legible chalk 2 + 2 and an offset = 4 below.
entries.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: ONE existing painted TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3 / 1776 Age of Revolutions.
Input image 1: the school blackboard icon to edit. Preserve this exact board design, natural wood colors, matte charcoal surface, frame, chalk ledge, chalk stick, attached legs and braces, perspective, lighting, texture, silhouette and transparent background. Do not redesign or add objects.
Primary request: Replace ONLY the random chalk strokes on the blackboard with one simple elementary arithmetic calculation. Completely remove ALL the old vertical and horizontal random lesson marks, while retaining the subtle underlying erasure smudges and matte surface.
Text (verbatim), first line: "2 + 2"
Text (verbatim), second line: "= 4"
Place the result line below the first, slightly offset to the right so the 4 is visibly displaced from the calculation. Both lines lie naturally on the same tilted blackboard plane, with correct perspective and sufficient clearance from the frame. Use large clear hand-written off-white chalk characters with slightly granular chalk texture and mild natural imperfection, not printed typography, raised carving, paper lettering or glossy paint.
The equation consists of exactly TWO numeral 2s, ONE plus sign, ONE equals sign and ONE numeral 4. All must be legible and spelled/rendered exactly. No other letters, numerals, words, random strokes, underline, border, arrows, doodles, heading or signature anywhere.
The user's explicit request for this legible calculation replaces the previous abstract-strokes-only constraint for the blackboard writing area. Do not apply a no-text rule to the requested equation.
Invariants: CHANGE ONLY THE CHALK WRITING. Keep the whole physical board and its small chalk stick unchanged as closely as possible. Neutral charcoal blackboard, warm brown wood, NO blue/teal color cast. No uniform sepia, new reflection, gold badge or frame around the icon.
Transparency: preserve genuine transparent alpha outside the object and through its structural gaps. The blackboard face is opaque dark material, NOT transparent. No black/white/checkerboard backdrop, classroom, floor or ground cast shadow. Whole feet and corners stay visible with generous margins, square high-resolution output.
Scope: the population register and optical telegraph are not edit targets and must not be altered. Output ONLY the edited blackboard icon, not a comparison sheet.

entries.subject: One broad open hand-bound population ledger with repeated handwritten entries and one quill, distinct from a sealed letter or blank book.
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE original TECHNOLOGY invention icon for the 1776 Age of Revolutions Victoria 3 mod. This is NOT a production-method flat pictogram, NOT a building scene and NOT a finished-good commodity icon.
Style: vanilla-compatible compact hand-painted volumetric object illustration. Clear broad masses, restrained matte brushwork and fine material grain, naturally differentiated material colors, soft upper-left light and subtly darker undersides. No glossy CGI, photorealistic still-life, flat vector, gold embossed badge, tiny landscape or steampunk fantasy.
Composition: one dominant object or coherent apparatus, at most one meaningful subordinate accessory. Modest three-quarter view with the object's defining face clearly visible. Entire silhouette, generous margins on all sides, square canvas at least 1024 px. Readable at 48 and 64 px without text. No cropped handles, corners or extremities.
Background: genuine transparent alpha around the object and through exterior openings. No fake black or white background, painted checkerboard, floor, table, ground, cast ground shadow, frame, circle, medallion, room or scenery. Contact shading between parts of the object is allowed.
Color: warm neutral wood, near-white ivory paper, dark iron and restrained brass details where mechanically needed. NO global blue/teal cast; no uniform sepia filter. No neon rim lighting. No actual readable letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, watermark, person or hands.
Historical references inform the concept but this is a simplified readable icon, not a certified artifact reconstruction. No modern plastics, electrical parts or invented ornament.
Primary subject: SYSTEMATIC POPULATION REGISTRATION, represented by ONE broad OPEN EIGHTEENTH-CENTURY POPULATION LEDGER, with ONE writing quill as the only meaningful accessory.
A thick rectangular hand-bound register lies open as an isolated object in a modest elevated three-quarter view. Two broad pale ivory pages, clearly joined at a central sewn gutter; natural brown leather cover visible around the lower edges; many thin paper leaves visible at the bottom side. It is one physically coherent book, not two detached sheets or two adjacent books. Strong broad open-book silhouette.
Across BOTH visible pages, repeated orderly record entries are shown in short horizontal rows, separated by fine understated rules and a narrow date margin. Use tiny irregular grey-brown ink marks to imply handwritten names and dates without any identifiable letters, words or numerals. No giant alphabet, illustration, calendar squares, spreadsheet UI, barcode or empty blank sheets. This repetitive registry layout is the defining subject, not ornate calligraphy.
ONE plain grey-white feather quill rests diagonally across the lower right edge, its cut writing tip pointing toward the central gutter and its upper feather visible beyond the right page. The quill is partly supported by the book, physically coherent, not impaled through a page. Simple off-white feather with a warm brown shaft, not a glossy oversized plume. Keep the book dominant and the records visible.
Paper is pale near-white ivory, wood/leather naturally brown, ink neutral charcoal. Restrained fine grain, real soft folds at the gutter, modest tonal shading; no uniform sepia and no blue highlights.
Historical reference: Aubervilliers municipal archives preserve bound baptism, marriage and burial registers covering October 1774 to August 1776. This icon is a conceptual administrative record book, not an exact facsimile of those registers; no real personal names or dates are copied.
No sealed envelope, wax seal, loose letter, ink bottle, separate pen holder, spectacles, rubber stamp, portrait, ruler, filing cabinet, tower, table, stage, pile of books or background.

entries.subject: An isolated Chappe optical semaphore mast, one central regulator and exactly two independent end indicators, working linked structure without a tower.
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE original TECHNOLOGY invention icon for the 1776 Age of Revolutions Victoria 3 mod. This is NOT a production-method flat pictogram, NOT a building scene and NOT a finished-good commodity icon.
Style: vanilla-compatible compact hand-painted volumetric object illustration. Clear broad masses, restrained matte brushwork and fine material grain, naturally differentiated material colors, soft upper-left light and subtly darker undersides. No glossy CGI, photorealistic still-life, flat vector, gold embossed badge, tiny landscape or steampunk fantasy.
Composition: one dominant object or coherent apparatus, at most one meaningful subordinate accessory. Modest three-quarter view with the object's defining face clearly visible. Entire silhouette, generous margins on all sides, square canvas at least 1024 px. Readable at 48 and 64 px without text. No cropped handles, corners or extremities.
Background: genuine transparent alpha around the object and through exterior openings. No fake black or white background, painted checkerboard, floor, table, ground, cast ground shadow, frame, circle, medallion, room or scenery. Contact shading between parts of the object is allowed.

Historical references inform the concept but this is a simplified readable icon, not a certified artifact reconstruction. No modern plastics, electrical parts or invented ornament.
Primary subject: OPTICAL TELEGRAPH, represented by the CHAPPE ARTICULATED SEMAPHORE MECHANISM, isolated and compact, no station building.
Mechanical construction MUST be physically coherent: ONE sturdy upright wooden mast supports the CENTRAL PIVOT of ONE long narrow regulator beam. The long regulator is tilted diagonally, rising from lower left to upper right.
At EACH END of that long regulator, an independent hinge supports ONE shorter narrow indicator arm. Exactly TWO short indicators, one on the left endpoint hinge and one on the right endpoint hinge. Both indicators in this chosen signal point upright, at visibly different angles relative to the tilted regulator. Thus exactly THREE signaling beams: one long centre-pivoted regulator plus two shorter END-pivoted indicators. Never attach all three at one central joint.
The regulator and indicators have broad dark charcoal-brown straight rectangular side rails with a restrained ladder-like row of small open gaps between slender cross slats, inspired by historical semaphore panels. Not four radial blades, a propeller, windmill, arrows, flags, modern traffic lights or railway signaling lights. Their small lattice openings have actual transparent alpha.
A few robust dark iron hinge pins and short paired cords with small dark counterweights below the two end hinges clarify connections. Taut fine control cords run beside the central mast down to ONE simple small hand crank/pulley fitted onto the lower mast. Do not draw stray loops or disconnected strings.
The mast terminates in a compact cross-foot of short structural wooden braces attached directly to it, enough to support the apparatus as an isolated object. This is a structural foot, NOT a tower, pedestal, floor or building. Shorten the mast for icon readability while preserving the three-beam mechanism and its connections. The upper signaling beams dominate the composition, the whole mechanism fills a compact roughly square silhouette. Entire two tips, joints and foot visible with generous margins.
Dark wood warm neutral brown, iron dark grey, only modest warm brass details at the crank if useful. Hand-painted volumetric style, natural material colors and restrained brush grain. No blue tint, polished brass miniature, gold medal or scenic outdoor view.
Reference examined: Musée des Arts et Métiers's Chappe optical-telegraph model, circa 1815, showing one regulator and two independent end indicators. The invention was presented in 1792. Use the verified linkage principle; the compact wood apparatus is a conceptual adaptation, not a claim to duplicate the museum's brass-and-marble physical model.
No communication wire across the picture, electric key, battery, watch face, clock, electrical equipment, map, paper message, flag, person, telescope, chimney, station house, horizon or scenery.
